reasons: Deviation is correctly characterized: the original clause is a symmetric consent regime with only a 'financially responsible affiliate' carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out for Client, an unqualified consent standard, and no competitor restriction on Vendor assignments — squarely short of the preferred position.

Redline reaches the playbook preferred position with all four required elements: Client free assignment to affiliates/successors in M&A or sale of substantially all assets, Vendor assignment subject to Client consent not unreasonably withheld, no assignment to a Client competitor, and express confirmation that a Client change of control creates no Vendor termination or re-pricing right.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.784 changed-character ratio) is justified here: converting a mutual consent prohibition into the asymmetric preferred structure necessarily requires rewriting the single sentence; no unrelated terms were touched.
Comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, explains the change and cites the fallback (mutual successor assignment with written notice) without lecturing.
Rationale correctly notes no 'change of control' language elsewhere in the Agreement, so no walk-away trigger; severity 'high' is consistent with the rule.
